evidence.exact_quote: Assert cmd.docker.host.instance.restart emits expected event type docker.host.instance_lifecycle_requested with command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target.

items.impact: A consumer can assert event type and dispatch correlation but cannot derive from this unit the operation discriminator, legal pre-state, resulting state, or rejected transition for restart.
items.statement: The restart oracle names the shared lifecycle event and correlation metadata, but the assigned unit does not expose an event payload field that identifies restart or a state-machine oracle for its precondition and completion transition.

evidence.exact_quote: cmd.docker.exec must be registered in the UICommand dispatcher with typed args and result contract
cmd.docker.host.instance.restart must emit the declared event types and record dispatch correlation evidence.

items.impact: Exec and restart can cross host authority boundaries or race concurrent lifecycle work; dispatcher typing and correlation alone do not falsify unauthorized targets, duplicate requests, partial completion, or recovery failure.
items.statement: The complete window supplies generic typed args/results and dispatch evidence but does not specify authorization scope, target validation, idempotency or concurrency policy, partial-failure states, or rollback/recovery behavior for Docker exec and restart.
items.title: Privileged exec and restart lack safety semantics

segments.summary: Reviewed all cancel/confirm/drift/exec/host-access/restart lines. Exact wiring and accessibility coverage is strong; lifecycle payload/state discrimination and privileged-operation authority, race, partial-failure, and recovery semantics are not exposed.

Reviewed all retain/start/stop/preflight/profile-save/receipt-open lines. Event and correlation oracles are explicit; lifecycle race/completion semantics and retention/profile data-policy boundaries remain unresolved in this unit.

Reviewed all host refresh/session/route and image/view/delete/inspect lines. The production-certification oracle is explicit, but image deletion and remote session launch lack destructive, authority, recovery, and terminal-lifecycle semantics.

Reviewed all image push/tag/inspect and Kubernetes apply/diff/exec lines. Receipt-only classification is explicit, while external-mutation completion/recovery and payload authorization/security boundaries are not defined here.

Reviewed all Helm install/preview, Kubernetes logs/port-forward/context/namespace, and Docker logs lines. Accessibility truth is explicit; transactional recovery, tunnel security/cleanup, selection propagation, and log privacy/scale semantics are absent from the unit.
